title: Periodic Inspection and Testing (Condition Reporting)
subtitle: Five Periodic Inspection and Condition Reporting practice tests
description: A merged advanced exam for periodic inspection, testing and condition reporting. It combines the periodic inspection bank with the EICR coding and reporting bank so each attempt tests both the inspection process and the final condition reporting judgement. Questions focus on GN3 intervals, sampling, limitations, dead/live testing, EICR documentation, C1/C2/C3/FI coding, PRS duties, duty-holder communication and defensible technical decisions.
format: Five rotating 40-question practice tests. Exam format: 60 minutes, open book (IET Guidance Note 3). Pass at 75%+.

scoring.label: Strong - exam-ready on GN3, EICR coding and defensible reporting
Pass - review missed interval, sampling, limitation or coding decisions
Needs targeted revision - re-read GN3 Chapter 3, BS 7671 Part 6 and BPG4
Major gaps - rebuild periodic inspection and condition reporting fundamentals first

priorities: C1, C2, C3 and FI must be applied from observed risk, not from how easy the remedial job looks.
Any C1, C2 or FI makes the EICR Unsatisfactory; C3 alone remains Satisfactory with improvement recommended.
Extent, sampling and limitations must be agreed, specific, recorded and revised when findings justify expansion.
Periodic inspection is judgement-led: select safe tests, justify live testing, and interpret readings against the existing installation condition.
Duty-holder and PRS duties matter: immediate danger notification, 28-day remedial rules, written confirmation and next-inspection recommendations.

questions.prompt: If an EICR for a rented dwelling identifies a C1 or C2 item, or requires further investigation, the landlord under the 2020 private rented sector electrical safety duties must normally arrange the required remedial or investigative work within:

options.A: 3 months
options.C: 28 days, or sooner if the report specifies a shorter period
options.D: 12 months

questions.explanation: For rented dwellings covered by the 2020 regulations in England, remedial or further investigative work must normally be completed within 28 days, unless the report specifies a shorter period. A C1 still needs immediate safety action; the legal 28-day period is not permission to leave danger present.

A.text: That would leave a known C2 or required investigation outstanding for about 90 days, well beyond the normal limit of 28 days. Any shorter period stated in the report applies, and a C1 must be made safe immediately.

B.text: Waiting for the next EICR could defer a known C2, C1 or FI concern for years. The rented-sector deadline is normally 28 days from the inspection, sooner when the report says so, with immediate danger made safe at once.

C.text: For rented dwellings covered by the 2020 regulations in England, remedial or further investigative work must normally be completed within 28 days, unless the report specifies a shorter period. A C1 still needs immediate safety action; the legal 28-day period is not permission to leave danger present.

D.text: A year-long delay is not allowed for a known safety finding. Required work is normally due within 28 days or the report's shorter period, while a C1 must be made safe immediately.

questions.prompt: A 20% sample of accessories is agreed for a 24-circuit office. On the first sampled socket circuit you find reversed polarity, loose CPCs and signs of overheating. What should happen to the sample?

options.A: Keep the 20% sample unchanged because it was agreed before work started
options.B: Increase the sample, potentially to 100% of that circuit and a greater sample of similar circuits

questions.explanation: Sampling is based on confidence. Early serious defects destroy confidence in the original sample. Reversed polarity and loose CPCs are normally C2, and overheating is usually C2 unless it presents immediate danger. The limitation should be revised or the client's refusal to expand the sample should be recorded.

A.text: 20 % is below the value produced by the stated data; the supported result is 100 %. Use each conductor's resistance per metre, its length and any parallel-path effect stated in the test method. Sampling is based on confidence.

questions.prompt: Which mapping best distinguishes N/V, LIM, FI and N/A?

options.D: N/V and FI mean exactly the same thing

questions.explanation: A limitation states an agreed or unavoidable restriction, N/V records an item that was not verified, and N/A means the item does not apply. FI is different: current Electrical Safety First guidance reserves it for a specific observed concern whose potential danger cannot be determined within the agreed inspection, not merely for every missing test or unidentified circuit.

A.text: The mapping confuses absence of evidence with danger: a locked roof void is LIM/N/V, a nonexistent pool is N/A, and connected sensitive equipment creates a stated test limitation. FI needs a specific unresolved possible danger.

B.text: A limitation states an agreed or unavoidable restriction, N/V records an item that was not verified, and N/A means the item does not apply. questions.prompt: The gas bonding conductor is present but connected 1.8 m downstream of the gas meter after a tee branch serving a boiler. The pipe enters the building in copper. What is the most defensible answer?

questions.prompt: At a three-phase distribution board, measured single-phase L-N prospective short-circuit current is 3.8 kA and L-E fault current is 2.9 kA. You cannot safely perform a line-line test. What should be recorded or estimated?

options.A: Only 2.9 kA, because earth faults are always the highest value
options.B: Only Ze, because PFC is not relevant at distribution boards
options.C: The average of 3.8 kA and 2.9 kA
options.D: Record the measured values and estimate maximum three-phase/line-line PFC where necessary, commonly as about 2 x L-N = 7.6 kA unless better data is available

questions.explanation: Three-phase boards may have a higher line-line or three-phase fault current than the line-earth fault current. If direct measurement is unsafe, use design data, DNO/manufacturer data or a justified estimate such as twice the measured single-phase L-N value.

A.text: A three-phase or line-to-line fault can exceed the measured single-phase value, so the report needs the measured figures plus a justified maximum estimate or better network data. The earth-fault reading is not automatically the highest; the larger measured short-circuit value governs the immediate breaking-capacity check.

B.text: A three-phase or line-to-line fault can exceed the measured single-phase value, so the report needs the measured figures plus a justified maximum estimate or better network data. Ze is an impedance, not the prospective current the protective device must interrupt; PFC is therefore essential at the distribution board.

C.text: A three-phase or line-to-line fault can exceed the measured single-phase value, so the report needs the measured figures plus a justified maximum estimate or better network data. Averaging hides the worst credible fault; equipment must be rated against the maximum prospective current, not the mean of two different fault modes.

D.text: Three-phase boards may have a higher line-line or three-phase fault current than the line-earth fault current. If direct measurement is unsafe, use design data, DNO/manufacturer data or a justified estimate such as twice the measured single-phase L-N value.

questions.prompt: A Type AC RCD protecting a circuit passes the standard AC residual-current trip test. The circuit supplies equipment likely to produce pulsating DC residual current components. What is the correct distinction?

options.D: RCD type is a design matter and must never be reported on an EICR

questions.explanation: A successful trip-time test proves operation only for the applied AC residual waveform; it does not prove the device is suitable for pulsating DC components from the load. Current Best Practice Guide 4 gives C3 where a Type AC RCD is installed where Type A is required, while an actual failed protective function is classified separately.

A.text: An AC-waveform trip test proves operation only for that test waveform; pulsating DC from the load can require a Type A or other suitable RCD even when the Type AC device trips on the tester. The test proves operation for the injected AC waveform only; it does not test whether connected electronics produce residual current the Type AC device can detect reliably.

B.text: An AC-waveform trip test proves operation only for that test waveform; pulsating DC from the load can require a Type A or other suitable RCD even when the Type AC device trips on the tester. The device operated on the specified test, so failure has not been shown; the issue is suitability for the load waveform and is normally C3 when Type A is required.

C.text: A successful trip-time test proves operation only for the applied AC residual waveform; it does not prove the device is suitable for pulsating DC components from the load. Current Best Practice Guide 4 gives C3 where a Type AC RCD is installed where Type A is required, while an actual failed protective function is classified separately.

D.text: An AC-waveform trip test proves operation only for that test waveform; pulsating DC from the load can require a Type A or other suitable RCD even when the Type AC device trips on the tester. An EICR assesses continued safety, including whether an existing protective device suits its connected load; design origin does not make that invisible.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Inspector confirms all circuits inspected and tested per the agreed scope; one C2 (missing main bonding) and three C3 (improvement recommendations)'. Outcome and duty holder action under PRS Regs 2020:

options.A: Satisfactory; no specific action required
options.B: Satisfactory subject to the client accepting the improvement recommendations
options.C: Pending until C3s addressed
options.D: Unsatisfactory because of the C2. Complete remedial work within 28 days of inspection, or any shorter period in the report; within 28 days of completion give the report and qualified-person confirmation to the tenant and local council. C3 items remain recommendations

questions.explanation: The C2 makes the report unsatisfactory. For a covered rented home in England, remedial work must be completed within 28 days of inspection or any shorter period stated in the report. Within 28 days of completion, the landlord gives the report and qualified-person confirmation to both the tenant and local council. C3 items remain improvement recommendations without that remedial deadline.
